name: Alaska

response.rule_text: Under the state agency regulations (2 AAC 96), the agency must furnish disclosable records within 10 working days; the statute itself sets no waiting period (AS 40.25.125 says no exhaustion required).

fees.labor_rule: Personnel costs for search and copying are chargeable only when production for one requester exceeds five person-hours in a calendar month, AS 40.25.110(c).
fees.copy_rule: Limited to the agency's 'standard unit cost of duplication', AS 40.25.110(b); electronic copies limited to actual incremental cost, AS 40.25.115(c).
fees.waiver_rule: Agencies may reduce or waive fees in the public interest, AS 40.25.110(d); copying charges of $5 or less may be waived.

residency.rule_text: Alaska law makes no distinction as to who may request public records.

appeal.body: Head of the agency that denied (state agencies, 2 AAC 96.345(c)); court suit allowed without exhausting remedies
appeal.rule_text: Denials of state-agency requests are appealed to the agency head, who must decide by the tenth working day after the record closes (2 AAC 96.345(a)); suit may be filed without exhaustion (AS 40.25.125). If no response arrives within a reasonable time after the limit, the request may be treated as denied (2 AAC 96.325(f)).

notes: Governor covered with deliberative-process/executive privilege caveat. Legislature records public via legislative rules and statutes, but enforceability doubtful (Abood). School boards 'clearly covered'. Appeal-to-agency-head deadline not found; 10-working-day response and 10-day extension come from RCFP's description of 2 AAC 96 regs, not statute. Unit 'working days' mapped to business.
